content:
Early-successional plant communities are characterized by rapid growth, high reproductive rates, and efficient resource use.  
Niche divergence (A) is more typical of stable, late-successional communities.  
K-selected species (C) are also more common in late-successional stages.  
High detrital biomass (D) accumulates later as communities mature.  
Early-successional species often have high productivity relative to biomass (B), due to fast growth and short life cycles.  

Final answer: (B)
